scalars.scalar_value: Minimum of 4 years laboratory/phlebotomy experience. Perform venous and/or skin punctures on adults.

items.item_text: High School graduation or GED
Minimum of 4 years laboratory/phlebotomy experience. Perform venous and/or skin punctures on adults.

Serves patients by identifying the best method of collecting blood samples and other specimens, asking relevant questions related to specimen collection, explains sampling procedures to patients, performs skilled, efficient venous and/or skin punctures, and prepares all specimens for the appropriate testing following established policies and procedures by the UCR Student Health Services Clinical Laboratory. Verifies test requisition and patient identification either electronically or on paper and bringing discrepancies to the attention of the CLS or Laboratory Supervisor. Be knowledgeable of the proper specimen handling and collection techniques and the correct order of draw. Perform computer entry of laboratory orders both in-house and send outs. Correctly processes all lab requisitions and forms for routine and reference testing. Receive specimens from patients and other medical staff and determines the acceptability of specimens for testing according to established criteria in testing procedures. Follows established company and department policies and procedures. Follows the guidelines for safety, environmental and infection control. Demonstrates a high level of integrity and honesty in maintaining confidentiality. Be able to uphold the UCR Principles of Community and the Standard of Ethical Conduct. (60% time)

Assists the CLS in the setup of CLIA-waved tests. Orders, monitors and maintains a consistent supply of phlebotomy consumables. Performs inventory of supplies and other consumables in a timely manner and communicates its status with appropriate personnel to ensure the availability of adequate supplies and to ensure no disruption in laboratory operations. Resolves unusual test orders by contacting the ordering physician or provider or calling the reference laboratory, referring unresolved orders back to the originator for further clarification and notifying the Laboratory Supervisor for unresolved orders. Promptly and courteously answers the phone and assists clients and other departments. Be respectful and always observe proper decorum, being mindful of the choice of words and tone of your voice. Maintains a cooperative working relationship with co-workers. Ensure a collaborative team-support working environment by assisting co-workers in the execution of their responsibilities whenever possible. Maintains professional growth and development through continuing education activities. (30% time)

Be able to clean and organize laboratory work area at the beginning and at the end of each shift by being able to discard specimens and dispose biohazard waste, accordingly, being always mindful of universal precautions. Participates in assisting the CLS in the introduction of new tests, procedures, and methodologies as well as in the training of new staff in the laboratory. Actively participates in all QI/QA projects and other related activities of the laboratory. Ensures compliance with relevant documentations supported by the laboratory including but not limited to submitting completed CMR reports to providers and to RPH, COVID results to state agencies, and other reportable documents, no shows report, scanning and sending results by Sfax, and other related responsibilities as may deemed necessary. Performs various clerical and other related miscellaneous tasks as assigned by the CLS and Laboratory Supervisor/Manager. (10% time)
Read/Comprehend: Constantly
Write: Frequently
Perform Calculations: Occasionally
Communicate Orally: Constantly
Reason & Analyze: Constantly
Bend: Occasionally
Sit: Frequently
Squat: Occasionally
Stand: Frequently
Walk: Frequently
Climb: Occasionally
Ability to maintain strict confidentiality and ability to have respect for all patients and co-workers with diverse cultural backgrounds and lifestyles.
Working knowledge of lab equipment and supplies. Orders, monitors and maintains a consistent supply of phlebotomy consumables.
Manual dexterity and visual and auditory acuity to perform the required duties.
Working knowledge of quality control principles and recordkeeping.
Familiarity with Standard (Universal) Precautions, handling of bio hazardous waste.
Familiarity with EMR Software (Point and Click) & LIS (Harvest-Orchard).
Ability to work quickly and accurately and to communicate, interact and be cooperative with patients and all personnel in the facility.

Ensures compliance with relevant documentations supported by the laboratory including but not limited to submitting completed CMR reports to providers and to RPH, COVID results to state agencies, and other reportable documents, no shows report, scanning and sending results by Sfax, and other related responsibilities as may deemed necessary.
Ability to write legibly and be attentive to details.
Performs various clerical and other related miscellaneous tasks as assigned by the CLS and Laboratory Supervisor/Manager.
Ability, on a daily basis, to assess overall workload for any area that needs help, and help co-workers without being reassigned by the supervisor.
Understanding of lab tests' clinical usefulness.
Ability to use good judgment in deciding when to seek clarification and assistance; be able to multi-task and to prioritize tasks in order of importance.
Ability to perform duties in a professional manner and put patients at ease.
Computer skills necessary to function in Windows application.
Be knowledgeable of the proper specimen handling and collection techniques and the correct Order of Draw.
Actively participates in all QI/QA projects and assisting the CLS in the introduction of new tests, procedures, and methodologies as well as in the training of new staff in the laboratory.
